verse.text: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
verse.summary: Psalm 147 was likely sung after the exiles came home and Jerusalem's walls went back up — the verse just before this one says the LORD "gathereth together the outcasts of Israel." And the very next line says He counts the stars and calls them all by name. The God who runs the galaxies stoops to the most private wound you carry, and He doesn't just heal the broken heart — He binds it, like a careful physician wrapping what still hurts while it mends. Whatever has been broken in you for a long time, He has not forgotten it, and He is not finished with it.

sermon.title: Wilt Thou Be Made Whole?
sermon.excerpt: Thirty-eight years by the pool, and somebody always reached the water first. Jesus stood over his mat and asked a question that sounds almost rude — wilt thou be made whole? — then bypassed the water entirely: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.

bibleStudy.title: She Loved Much

verses.text: And, behold, a woman in the city, which was a sinner, when she knew that Jesus sat at meat in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster box of ointment, And stood at his feet behind him weeping, and began to wash his feet with tears, and did wipe them with the hairs of her head, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the ointment. Now when the Pharisee which had bidden him saw it, he spake within himself, saying, This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner.

And he turned to the woman, and said unto Simon, Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head. Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet. My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment. Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

bibleStudy.excerpt: Simon gave Jesus a seat at his table and nothing else. A woman the whole town had a name for gave Him her tears, her hair, and her last shred of reputation — and only one of them actually loved Him.
body: Start with what Simon didn't do, because the omission is the whole sermon before anyone says a word. He invited Jesus to dinner — bold move, give him that — but Luke tells you three separate things Simon left undone: no water for the dust on his guest's feet, no kiss of greeting at the door, no oil for his head. None of those three were luxuries in that culture; they were the bare minimum, the stuff you didn't even have to think about for a guest you actually wanted in your house. Simon skipped all three on purpose or by sheer indifference — Scripture doesn't say which, and honestly it doesn't matter, because both add up to the same verdict: he wanted Jesus close enough to examine, not close enough to touch.

Then a woman nobody invited let herself in, and Luke doesn't soften the introduction one bit: "a woman in the city, which was a sinner." No name, no biography, just a reputation that apparently preceded her through the whole town, because the second she walks in, Simon doesn't think "who is this," he thinks "I already know exactly who this is." "This man, if he were a prophet, would have known who and what manner of woman this is that toucheth him: for she is a sinner." Notice the logic — Simon isn't wrong about her file. He's wrong about what a prophet is supposed to do with it. He assumes holiness means keeping your distance from a mess like her. Jesus, who actually was the Prophet, knew her file better than Simon did and let her keep touching Him anyway.

Look at what she actually does, because it costs her everything she has left to lose. She stands behind Him weeping — not a polite, controlled tear, but enough of them to wash dusty feet. She wipes them with her hair, which in that world was not a hairstyle, it was a scandal; a woman let her hair down in public for exactly one kind of audience, and it was never a room full of Pharisees at dinner. She kisses His feet, and she empties out an alabaster box of ointment that likely cost her more than Simon's whole table setting. This is a woman with nothing left to protect — no reputation left to ruin, no dignity left to spend — pouring the only currency she had left onto a pair of feet nobody else in that house would even touch.

Jesus answers Simon's silent judgment with a two-sentence story, because sometimes a parable lands where an argument never could. Two men owed a moneylender — one owed five hundred pence, the other fifty, and neither one of them could pay back a cent of it. The creditor forgave them both outright, wiped both ledgers clean, no payment plan, no probation. "Tell me therefore," Jesus says, "which of them will love him most?" And Simon, without realizing he's about to indict himself, gives the correct answer: "I suppose that he, to whom he forgave most." Thou hast rightly judged, Jesus tells him — and then turns Simon around to watch the parable walk itself around the room in real time.

"Seest thou this woman?" — four words that should stop every reader cold, because Simon had been staring at her all night and genuinely never seen her. "I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head. Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet. My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment." Three omissions, three extravagances, laid side by side so nobody in that room could pretend the math was close. Simon gave Jesus a seat. She gave Him everything she owned and everything she was ashamed of, in the same motion.

Then comes the verse that gets misquoted in every direction except the right one: "Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little." Read that wrong and you'll think she earned her forgiveness by crying hard enough, loving extravagantly enough, performing devotion impressively enough — as if tears are currency and she simply paid more than Simon did. That's backwards. Her sins are forgiven, already, a settled fact by the time she walks through that door weeping. She isn't loving her way into pardon. She's weeping her way out of gratitude for a pardon she already has. Simon's problem was never that his sin tally was actually lower than hers — it's that he never believed he had much of a tally to begin with, so forgiveness landed on him like a small kindness instead of a rescue, and a small kindness produces a small love every single time.

Here's my real question for you today, and I need you to actually answer it instead of filing it under "interesting sermon point": are you loving Jesus like Simon, or like the woman? Simon's version shows up on time, keeps its manners, never once gets dirt under its fingernails, and privately keeps score of everybody else's mess because it has long since stopped noticing its own. Her version shows up uninvited, weeping, unconcerned with who's watching, because somewhere along the way she actually grasped what she'd been forgiven for. You cannot manufacture her kind of love by trying harder to look devoted. You can only receive it, the way you receive a debt you genuinely could not pay being genuinely cancelled — and then watch what that does to your Monday mornings, your prayer life, your willingness to be seen loving Him loudly in a room full of people still keeping score.

Paul says in one sentence what this whole dinner party took an evening to demonstrate: "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us." Not after we cleaned up. Not once we qualified. While. The cross was never a reward for the people who kept their nose clean enough to deserve it — if it were, Simon would've been first in line and the woman wouldn't have made the guest list at all. Instead heaven ran the math the exact opposite way the Pharisee did: the five-hundred-pence debtor and the fifty-pence debtor both got the same zero balance, which is either wildly unfair or it's the gospel, and it is not the first one.

So stop auditing her and start checking your own guest list for Jesus. Have you let Him close enough to actually touch, or just close enough to seat at your table and study from a safe, respectable distance? Whatever reputation you're carrying that makes you think you don't belong this close to Him — the city already knew hers, and He let her stay anyway. Come weeping if you have to. Come uninvited if that's the only way you'll come. Bring whatever's left in your alabaster box, because the posture that's never once impressed heaven is Simon's composed hospitality, and the posture that silenced a whole room was one broken woman who finally understood how much she'd been forgiven. Go and love much, because you were forgiven much. In Jesus' name, amen.

lines: Father, I declare today that I will be made whole — I am done making peace with what You came to heal!
You saw me lying there, and You knew how long — not one year of my waiting was hidden from You!
The length of my wait does not set the length of my deliverance!
I have no man — but I have the Son of Man, and He does not need the water to move!
When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up!
No one will step down before me into what God has written for me!
I rise! I take up my bed! I walk!
What used to carry me, I now carry as a testimony!
He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds — and that includes mine!
Save this. Speak it over your house today. Rise, take up thy bed, and walk — I will be made whole! In Jesus' mighty name, amen!

dreamFire.title: Only His Word Stands Tonight
dreamFire.intro: Tonight's shield prayer is not about any one dream scene — it meets every curse spoken over you, every verdict passed against you, every decree muttered at a dark table while you slept. Whatever voice tried to speak last night, it does not get the final word over your life. Pray this aloud before you close your eyes, in Jesus' name.
points: Father, Your Word declares in Isaiah 8:10, "Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us" — every counsel gathered against me in the dream realm tonight, every word spoken to establish evil over my life, comes to nought and cannot stand, for God is with me, in the mighty name of Jesus!

By the authority of Numbers 23:19, "God is not a man, that he should lie...hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?" — I decree that only what God has spoken over my life shall stand; every lying word, every false decree uttered against me while I slept is exposed as a lie and has no power to make itself good, in Jesus' mighty name!

Father, as it is written in Job 22:28, "Thou shalt also decree a thing, and it shall be established unto thee: and the light shall shine upon thy ways" — I decree light, not darkness, over my destiny tonight, and I cancel every decree the enemy tried to establish against me in my sleep; only my decree, rooted in Your Word, stands, in the mighty name of Jesus!

I stand on Proverbs 26:2, "As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come" — every curse spoken against me tonight is causeless, for I am redeemed and covered by the blood; let it fly on and find no resting place on my head, my home, or my family, in the mighty name of Jesus!

By the Word in Proverbs 18:21, "Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof" — I silence every tongue that spoke death over me in a dream tonight; I decree only life, and every evil speaker shall eat the fruit of their own wicked words, in Jesus' mighty name!

I decree by Isaiah 55:11, "So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please..." — I send Your Word against every evil word released over me tonight; Your Word shall accomplish what You please, and every contrary word returns to its sender void, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, by the promise in Jeremiah 1:12, "Thou hast well seen: for I will hasten my word to perform it" — hasten Your word of life over my sleep tonight, and let every hastened plan of darkness be frustrated and delayed, in Jesus' mighty name!

Father, as in Psalm 107:20, "He sent his word, and healed them, and delivered them from their destructions" — send Your word now into every place a dream of destruction tried to touch my body, my mind, or my future, and let me be healed and delivered completely, in the mighty name of Jesus!

I stand on Psalm 119:89, "For ever, O LORD, thy word is settled in heaven" — no midnight decree, no witchcraft verdict, no dream tribunal can edit what is already settled in heaven concerning me; Your Word outranks every voice raised against me tonight, in Jesus' mighty name!

By the authority Christ gave me in Mark 11:23, "Whosoever shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea...he shall have whatsoever he saith" — I speak to every mountain of evil decree raised against me in the dream realm: be thou removed and cast into the sea, in the mighty name of Jesus!

Father, Your Word declares in Matthew 24:35, "Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away" — every dream-word spoken to alter my destiny shall pass away and be forgotten, but Your Word concerning my life stands forever, in the mighty name of Jesus!

So I seal tonight with Psalm 138:2, "...thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name" — every name invoked against me in the dream realm tonight, every title, every altar, every tribunal, bows to the Name above every name, because His Word outranks them all. I will wake in the morning carrying only the word He has spoken over me — untouched, unshaken, and unafraid — in the mighty, all-consuming name of Jesus Christ, amen! 🔥
